title: Physics Methodology
purpose: Seed physics-specific methodology so Lantern can connect mathematical models to calibrated measurement, use dimensions/conservation/symmetry as constraints, reason with idealizations and approximation regimes, and distinguish theoretical, experimental and computational evidence.

concepts.definition: A measurable property represented by magnitude, dimension/unit and uncertainty under an operational procedure.
A mathematical/conceptual representation of a physical system with assumptions, state variables, parameters and applicability regime.
Development/analysis of mathematical frameworks/models and their consequences, constrained by consistency and empirical testability where applicable.
Designed measurement/intervention used to test physical predictions, determine parameters or discover phenomena.
Numerical simulation/computation used when analytic solutions are unavailable/impractical; results remain conditional on equations, algorithms, approximations and inputs.
Use of physical dimensions to constrain equations, conversions and scaling relationships.
A physical regularity asserting invariance of a quantity under specified system conditions/scope.
Invariance of a physical description under a transformation; symmetries can constrain allowed models and relate to conservation structures.
Intentional simplification such as point mass, frictionless plane or ideal gas used within a defined approximation purpose.
Range of parameters/conditions where a simplified model approximates a more general description to acceptable accuracy.
Specified conditions needed with governing equations to determine/predict system behavior.
Inference of model parameters from measurements with uncertainty and model assumptions.
High-accuracy comparison of a model prediction against measurement to constrain deviations/parameters.
Failure to detect a predicted/new effect within stated sensitivity, producing bounds rather than automatically proving exact absence.
Relationship describing how a physical quantity changes with scale/parameters under specified regime.
Approximate scale reasoning useful for feasibility, plausibility and dominant-effect estimation.
Quantification of how input measurement/parameter uncertainty contributes to uncertainty in a derived physical result.
Structured uncertainty from calibration, environment, model/instrument effects or analysis that does not vanish by simple repetition.

guards.reason: Dimensional consistency is necessary for many physical equations but not sufficient for empirical correctness.
A coherent mathematical model may not describe the physical world.
Idealizations are deliberate simplifications, not necessarily literal descriptions.
Numerical output is conditional on model, algorithm and inputs.
A null result generally constrains effects below detection/sensitivity rather than proving exact zero.
Precision improves comparison but model validity depends on prediction agreement and assumptions.
Conservation statements depend on system boundaries/symmetry/conditions.
Multiple models can fit finite data; prediction, mechanism, parsimony and new tests matter.
Methods appropriate to physical quantities need not answer historical, interpretive or social questions.

invariants: Physical claims connect mathematical structure to operationally defined measurement.
Dimensions constrain meaningful equations but do not prove empirical truth.
Models preserve assumptions, parameters, initial/boundary conditions and applicability regimes.
Idealizations are tools whose usefulness depends on approximation error and purpose.
Theoretical consistency, computational simulation and experimental measurement are distinct evidence/method types.
Precision tests compare predictions and measurements with uncertainty on both model/parameter and measurement sides where applicable.
Null results produce sensitivity-dependent constraints rather than automatic exact-zero conclusions.
Systematic uncertainty cannot be removed merely by more repeated measurements.
Order-of-magnitude reasoning supports plausibility/feasibility but is not exact calculation.
Physics methodology is domain-specific and must not be projected as the sole scientific method.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core methodology of theoretical, experimental and computational physics, dimensional analysis, measurement science, approximation and precision testing adapted to Lantern's scientific architecture.
